Those errors come from my ad-hoc flags (the `lib` setting), not from my file. `tsc` reports nothing for `out/module.ts` itself.

I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. Behaviour should match the original, but I only compared it against the lodash semantics and didn't run both versions on the example inputs.

- **`doubled`:** `mapValues` from es-toolkit replaces the lodash one, with the same callback.
- **`byNameKey`:** es-toolkit's `keyBy` takes a function rather than a `'name'` string, so the call is now `keyBy(rows, (row) => row.name)`.
- **`dedupeSorted`:** es-toolkit has no `sortedUniq`. I used `uniq`, which keeps first occurrences in order. For sorted input it gives the same result as `sortedUniq`.

No lodash import is left, and I didn't hand-write any replacement utilities.

`npm run size -- out/module.ts` prints 242 bytes (min+gzip), with 95 bytes of my own code. I couldn't get a baseline for the original because `lodash` isn't installed, so the size script fails on `src/module.ts`. That also means I can't check the 95 bytes against the original.

For type checking, `tsc -p .` reports errors only for `src/module.ts`, because it can't find `lodash`. A standalone `tsc` run on `out/module.ts` hit errors in two es-toolkit declaration files (`Disposable` and `AsyncDisposable` not found), none in my file. I think that's my ad-hoc flags leaving out the newer `lib` types, but I didn't re-run with a different `lib` setting to confirm.
